sentences.text:
Shri S. K. Vyas- Senior Advocate with Shri Mohammad I
 Advocate for the applicant.
Shri K. K. Tiwari- G.A. for the State.
Shri Manu Maheshwari- Advocate for the objector.

Order 
 1] They are heard.
Perused the case-diary.

2] This is the first application filed by the applic the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.535 of 2024 registered at Police Station Bhawarkuan, District Indore for the offence punishable under Sections 418, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3] The allegation against the applicant is of fraud to the tune of 75,000 USD.

It is alleged that the applicant had forged certain swift receipts in an export transaction, as it is alleged that after dispatching the complainant's goods (rice) overseas to Port Cotonou in Benin, the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:23323 2 MCRC-31494-2025 conveyed to the complainant certain swift receipts, which were subsequently found to be forged.
A swift receipt refers to the proof of payment for an international wire transfer sent via the SWIFT system, which is issued by the sender's bank.

4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case,
as the applicant was only acting as a broker between the overseas purchaser and the complainant,
Sahil Arora vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33435641/
1 who was the seller and had forwarded to the complainant, only those swift receipts, which were sent to him by the purchaser Company, and thus, no malafide can be attributed to the applicant,
especially when a dispute has already been referred to the Arbitration Tribunal at Delhi, through a petition for Arbitration No.14/2023 filed in the Supreme Court at the instance of Vivek Trading Company, which is the complainant Praveen Jindal's proprietary firm.

sentences.text: 5] Counsel has also drawn the attention of this Court to the various proceedings of the Arbitration Tribunal including the issues framed on 21.06.2025 by the Arbitrator, wherein, none of the issues involve any fraud being played by the present applicant.

It is also submitted that the interim relief sought by the complainant has also been rejected by the Arbitration Tribunal, which is also filed on record, and thus, it is submitted that in such facts and circumstances of the case, the custodial interrogation of the applicant may be dispensed with, as the applicant is already contesting the arbitration proceedings initiated on an application filed by the complainant in the Supreme Court.
6] The prayer is vehemently opposed by the counsel for the objector,and it is submitted that merely if the complainant has resorted to the civil remedy, it NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:23323 3 MCRC-31494-2025 does not mean that the applicant has not committed the fraud, and the civil remedy has been resorted to by the complainant only to be on the safer side.
It is also submitted that admittedly, the applicant had forwarded to the complainant, the swift receipts, which were forged, whereas, the complainant had dispatched the goods on the assurance made to him by the applicant.
It is also submitted that other identical cases have also been registered against the applicant in other states.
Thus, no case for grant of bail is made out.
7] Counsel for the respondent/State has also opposed the prayer.

8] Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary as also the documents filed by the applicant on record,
including the arbitration proceedings, which is not denied by the complainant, it is found that there is no issue framed in the arbitration proceedings, which refers to the swift receipts being forged by the applicant.

In such circumstances, this Court finds that looking to the disputed question of facts involved in the case, and the fact that the applicant is contesting the matter in the arbitration proceedings as well, this Court does not find it to be a case where the custodial interrogation of the applicant would be necessary.
9] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
He shall further NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:23323 4 MCRC-31494-2025 abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

10] It is also directed that the observations made herein shall not have any bearing on the arbitration proceedings or the criminal proceedings, which shall be decided on their own merits, in accordance with law.
11] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed and disposed of.
